answer: Each live key may custody only one serialized assay ingot—the scarce relic—inside a bonded bullion vault whose locker count is hard-capped by the assay office. Enrollment welds the ingot's metallurgical grain hash and locker number to a single signing key, then publishes that binding on a public inclusion trellis. Random audits require a signed locker-camera frame plus a fresh X-ray grain match; a second key on the same locker is slashed. Because lockers and ingots cannot be shared, every fake identity needs its own ingot and vault slot, so attacker cost grows at least linearly.
